messages:
emma_support: FYI - escalation from ACME-Pay. Their JSON-mode endpoint started failing after a routing fallback. They see parser errors: 'missing items[0].id' and customer says it used to work.
sanjay_eng: Can you paste the failing response and the original request? Also which model/variant we routed to?
emma_support: Pasted below (sanitized). They call /v1/complete with mode=json and a schema expecting items[].id. Request body is standard. Response we got back after routing -> quant-variant-1:
```
{"order_id":"ord_93","items":[],"total":12.50}
```
Expected:
```
{"order_id":"ord_93","items":[{"id":"sku_123","qty":1}],"total":12.50}
```
So items array is present but empty. Parser fails because downstream validation requires items[0].id.

devon_ml: Interesting — upstream trace shows a fallback to `gptq-1a` around 2026-11-03T14:22:10Z due to capacity. That variant has an output-wrapping shim in our runtime to preserve tokens when quantized. Could be removing short arrays.
lena_qa: Can reproduce locally by forcing the routing rule to use the quantized fallback. Repro steps I'm using below.

lena_qa: Repro steps (quick):
```
# hit hosted endpoint forcing variant via X-Model-Variant header
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/complete \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Model-Variant: gptq-1a" \
  -d '{"prompt":"generate order json","mode":"json","schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"order_id":{"type":"string"},"items":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"id":{"type":"string"}}}}}}'}
```
Response is often `{"order_id":"ord_x","items":[],"total":...}` or sometimes a prose wrapper.

sanjay_eng: Can you attach the runtime logs for the request that fell back? Need the exchange between router and executor. @ops_rachel FYI — any recent routing policy change or model swap around that timestamp?
ops_rachel: deploy-bot shows a canary swap of variant pools at 2026-11-03T14:20:00Z (autoscale trigger). No config change to JSON handling. But I do see a model artifact update pushed by infra for gptq-1a with a different tokenizer mapping.

devon_ml: Tokenizer changes could lead to different decoding heuristics; but dropping array contents is more likely a postprocessing hook in the quantized executor to coalesce empty prefixes. I'll run a focused test to dump raw tokens + decoded string before our JSON sanitizer.

emma_support: Customer reported this started after a 'capacity reroute' message in their logs. They have business impact — parser rejects payloads and 4xx returned to them. Customer wants rollback to previous routing variant until we fix.

lena_qa: Quick mitigation: we can add a temporary lenient validation at the API layer that treats empty items array as a soft-fail and attempts a retry with `X-Fallback-Disable: true` header to force non-quant variant. Tested: retry succeeds 90% in my run.

sanjay_eng: Good. Plan: 1) surface mitigation to Support to enable per-customer retry header, 2) collect failing request IDs and raw token dumps from executor, 3) rollback gptq-1a artifact if token-diff shows regression. @devon_ml take lead on token diffs. @ops_rachel can you stage rollback option?

devon_ml: On it. I'll post token-diff blames within 2 hours. Also attaching a quick script to reproduce token dump locally.
```
# repro-token-dump (python)
# - send request with X-Model-Variant
# - capture /executor/raw_tokens endpoint
```

emma_support: Thanks — passing mitigation and repro steps to ACME-Pay. They're going to enable the retry header for now. I'll keep posting updates here. :pray:
